# Effect: plugin

Third-party plugin effect (VST3/CLAP/LV2).

**Where to put it**: Sits in the chain like a built-in effect. path is the absolute path of the plugin on this machine; params are set by plugin parameter name, and a value may be the text shown in the plugin UI (e.g. "2000 Hz"). Use `muser plugin params <path>` to list the parameters.

Latest parameters: `muser effects plugin` (MCP: `describe_effect`)

## Fields

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `path` | Required, absolute path of the plugin file or bundle (.vst3 / .clap / .lv2) |
| `id` | Optional, plugin id |
| `params` | Optional, `{ parameter id: value }` |

## Minimal example

```json
{ "type": "plugin", "path": "/usr/lib/clap/Surge XT Effects.clap", "params": { "FX Type": "Reverb 2" } }
```

## Tips and common mistakes

- path is an absolute path on this machine; common directories: /usr/lib/vst3, ~/.vst3, /usr/lib/clap, ~/.clap, /usr/lib/lv2.
- When one plugin file contains several plugins, specify one with `id`; if omitted, the first is used.
- `params` uses the plugin parameter **names** as keys (case-insensitive; a numeric id also works), and the value is the text the plugin displays (such as "2000 Hz", "Reverb 2"), a number (plugin automation scale), or true/false.
- To look up parameters: `muser plugin params <path> --filter <keyword>`; the selectable texts of an option-type parameter: `muser plugin values <path> <parameter name>`; when a parameter's effect is unclear, audition it with `muser audition --effect ... --param ...`. See [plugins.md](../plugins.md) for the full flow.
- Plugin parameters can be automated: `{ "target": "effects[0]", "param": "<plugin parameter name>", ... }`, and the values can likewise be written as text.
- Loading a plugin runs third-party code; use only trusted plugins on this machine.
